definition: Segment Anything is a series of open-source computer vision foundation models developed by Meta AI (formerly Facebook AI Research, and later Meta Superintelligence Labs) for image and video segmentation.
details: The project was introduced in April 2023 with the Segment Anything Model (SAM), a promptable segmentation model trained on the SA-1B dataset of over 1.1 billion masks, and has since been extended by SAM 2 (2024), which unified image and video segmentation, and SAM 3 (2025), which added segmentation from natural-language concept prompts. The models are released under the Apache 2.0 license and have been widely adopted in research and industry, including medical imaging, earth observation, robotics, and content editing tools.

explainer.lead: Segment Anything is a series of open-source computer vision foundation models from Meta AI for image and video segmentation. It matters because a single promptable model has been widely adopted across research and industry.

tiers.eli5: It is like a smart highlighter that can outline any object you point at in a picture or video.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to segment objects in images and video, now also from natural-language concept prompts. A pitfall is that results still depend on how the prompt is given and on the domain.

explainer.example: A user gives a point or concept prompt on an image, and the model returns a mask outlining the corresponding object.
